interest: Matsuoka's 1940 purge of the Foreign Office and Japan's turn south.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.021, covering February 1940 to May 1942) documents the organization, internal personnel changes, and sweeping institutional reforms of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Gaimushō) and its overseas diplomatic corps leading up to and during the early months of the Pacific War. The primary focus of the collection is the dramatic August-September 1940 reorganization and ideological purge executed by newly installed Foreign Minister Yōsuke Matsuoka following the inauguration of the second Konoe cabinet. Through diplomatic despatches, telegrams from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo and consular officers in China and the Netherlands East Indies, and State Department cross-reference sheets, the file records the dismissal and forced retirement of senior career diplomats aligned with Great Britain and the United States, their replacement by nationalist and pro-Axis figures, the appointment of Lieutenant General Yoshitsugu Tatekawa to Moscow to negotiate a rapprochement with the USSR facilitating Japan's 'Southward Advance,' the diplomatic buildup accompanying the recognition of the Wang Jingwei regime in Nanking, and wartime intelligence on the ministry's structural hierarchy.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew clarifies the true status of Kunryo Obata, a Japanese Foreign Office employee who misrepresented himself to New York Times correspondent Hallett Abend in Shanghai as an influential diplomat.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Grew identifies 'K. Obata', who spoke to Hallett Abend, as Kunryo Obata, a minor propaganda employee of the Information Bureau with little authority.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4539 from Grew (Tokyo) on Identity and Status of Kunryo Obata

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 39 from Nanking regarding the transfer of Consul General T. Hori to the Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Stanton's telegram No. 39: Consul General Hori leaving Nanking for the Foreign Office.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram No. 39 from Stanton (Nanking)

subfiles.about: Consul Stanton reports on Japanese diplomatic changes in Nanking, including the transfer of Consul General Hori and arrangements for opening the Japanese Embassy under General Abe.
subfiles.from: Edwin F. Stanton, U.S. Consul at Nanking
subfiles.summary: Stanton reports Hori handing over at Nanking to Y. Hanawa as the consulate becomes Japan's Embassy to the Wang Jingwei government, with General Abe due.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 39 from Stanton (Nanking) on Diplomatic Reorganization and Embassy Opening

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 776 from Tokyo regarding Japanese Foreign Office and Foreign Service personnel changes.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram No. 776 from Grew (Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports official gazetted appointments, transfers, voluntary resignations, and dismissals across the Japanese Foreign Office and diplomatic corps.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Grew lists Foreign Office appointments and resignations from the Official Gazette, September 1940, including Kumaichi Yamamoto and Itaro Mizuno, and Minister Sotomatsu Kato's removal.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 776 from Grew (Tokyo) on Official Gazette Diplomatic Appointments and Resignations

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 767 from Tokyo concerning detailed personnel changes in the Japanese Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram No. 767 from Grew (Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports on Foreign Minister Matsuoka's sweeping shake-up of career diplomats to eliminate Western-leaning personnel and install nationalist officials aligned with Axis policy.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Matsuoka's sweeping Foreign Office shake-up of August 1940: senior envoys resign, seniority is ignored, and pro-Axis, nationalist diplomats are favored over those tied to Britain and America.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 767 (Sections 1 & 2) from Grew on Matsuoka's Foreign Service Shake-up and Ideological Shift

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram No. 737 from Grew (Tokyo)

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram No. 820 from Grew (Tokyo)
